title: Tess the Otter's Honest Words
markdown:
Tess the otter loved writing for the Woodland Weekly. But today, her tummy did a flip-flop! It was Market Day, and she had to interview everyone. "Oh dear," she squeaked, "What if my words get all wobbly?"

The market was a happy jumble of sunshine and chatter. Tess took a deep breath and waddled to Farmer Giles.

"Hello!" she chirped. "I'm Tess Otter! How are your apples?"

Farmer Giles beamed. "These aren't just apples, Tess! They're sun-kissed jewels, full of summer smiles!"

Tess scribbled, "Sun-kissed jewels! Wowee!"

Next, Penelope the pigeon fluffed her feathers. "My seeds," she cooed, "are tiny promises of yummy feasts! Listen closely, you can hear a sprout wishing for the sun!"

Tess’s pencil zoomed. "Tiny universes! Whispers of tomorrow's bread!"

Mr. Badger called his honey "liquid sunshine." Mrs. Squirrel said her nuts were "nature's treasure chests!" Everyone made ordinary things sound like magic!

Tess came to Miss Lane's bakery. Warm, sweet smells filled the air. Miss Lane, a kind badger, arranged berry tarts.

"Miss Lane," Tess said softly, "your tarts look so yummy! What are they?"

Miss Lane smiled. "These are just berry tarts, Tess. Made with berries, sugar, and butter. And love."

Tess's heart wobbled. "But... not sun-kissed jewels?"

Miss Lane chuckled. "No, dear. Love is the best ingredient. Sometimes, simple truth, told with a kind heart, is the biggest treasure."

Just then, Hugo the rabbit hopped by. "Hello, Tess! How's the reporting?"

Tess sighed. "Everyone else's things are magic! Mine will be plain. Berries are just berries."

Hugo twitched his nose. "Plain? Tess, you tell us what things *are*! When you say 'juicy berries,' we know they'll taste like summer! That's not plain, that's super helpful!"

Miss Lane nodded. "Hugo's right. Your honest words are like a guiding star. We trust you because you tell true stories."

Tess looked at her notepad, then at the tarts, then at Hugo's kind face. A big smile spread across her face. She *did* tell things clearly. Her way was special too!

"Thank you, Miss Lane! Thank you, Hugo!" she said, her voice bright. "I know just what to write! My words can be treasures too!"

Tess finished her report. It wasn't filled with jewels or moonbeams. It told of the ripest berries, crunchiest nuts, and warmest bread, with Tess's own clear, honest words. Everyone agreed. Tess’s report was a treasure, because it was honest, helpful, and written with the brave heart of Tess the otter. She wiggled her tail. Tess the otter was a reporter, and she was great at it!
characters: Tess the otter, Hugo the rabbit, Miss Lane
